items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The visible code is clear. Type names are consistent (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie), fields have doc comments covering dedup and ordering, and ptr.Deref is used for defaults. Logic is in its own consistent_hash.go file.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: a separate consistent_hash.go plus a merge function. Generated code came from `make go-generate-apis`, not hand edits. Unit tests and golden tests were added, and `make analyze` is clean. No debug leftovers are visible.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The CRD bounds inputs with MinLength/MaxLength/MaxItems and a TTL pattern. A bad cookie TTL is reported as a policy error, and a bad regexRewrite is caught in Validate. Nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: The golden merge output shows the higher-priority X-Tenant header before x-user, deduplicated and re-sorted (headers, then cookie, then queryParameter). Metadata lists both policies under merge.TrafficPolicy...consistentHash. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule `!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers)...)` is in the generated CRD. The golden output shows the `{}` default as a single connectionProperties sourceIp entry with no terminal. A consistent-hash-disable golden test covers disable at rule level.
